newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt up on Argentine global issue demand.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt up on Argentine global issue demand.

text.p: Emerging debt tightened to U.S. Treasuries by 10 to 20 basis points on Wednesday, largely because of strong bidding for Argentina's freshly priced $2.0 billion global issue, traders said.
Prices rose strongly much of the day but came off their highs in late-afternoon trading as U.S. Treasuries dipped, they said.

The Argentine issue priced at 462.5 basis points over Treasuries, compared with earlier price talk of 475 to 500 basis points. The tighter pricing resulted from strong demand and a 3.5-times oversubscription.
With a coupon of 11.375 percent, the issue priced at 99.416 to yield 11.45 percent.
Enthusiasm for the new Argentine debt and the recent $1 billion 10-year Mexican global issue has cheered market participants who were concerned about how easily the new supply might be digested.
The Argentine global, after it was freed to trade at par, quickly traded as high as 102-1/4.
"Right now the market is focusing particularly on Argentina," said Kurt Schmid, executive vice president and head of propietary trading at SBC Warburg.
And that attention resulted in "activity in other benchmark assets in Argentina, as well as Brazil 'C' bonds and Mexico," Schmid added.
At 1500 EST/2000 GMT, Argentine pars were 3/8 firmer at 64-3/4 bid, while that country's FRBs and discount bonds were unchanged.
Mexican discounts were 3/8 of a percentage point higher at 92 bid and Brazil "C" bonds were 1/4 firmer at 76-5/8 bid.

Panama PDI bonds turned in the most dramatic rally, climbing nearly 6.0 percentage points after Panama Brady bonds received ratings of BB-plus from Moody's Investors Service and Ba1 from Standard & Poor's Corp.
"The rating change and a lack of supply" drove prices up, one trader said. At 1500 EST/2000 GMT, PDIs were up 5-5/8 at 88-1/8 bid.
While some traders saw room for more appreciation in PDI prices, SBC's Schmid questioned whether fundamentals justify current price levels in the overall market in general and PDIs in specific.

"The question is whether, in a relatively difficult U.S. interest rate environment, such tremendous appreciation overall is justified or whether it is just a lot of demand chasing a little bit of supply," Schmid said.
"Such a dramatic appreciation of (PDI) prices was somewhat surprising and unexpected," he added.
More broadly, Bulgarian IABs were up 3/8 at 52-5/8 bid, while Russian dollar Vnesh were unchanged at 79-3/4 bid after giving up gains scored earlier in Europe.
